explanation: Keep prices in an OrderedDict from least recent to most recent. A successful lookup or insertion of an existing ISBN moves that entry to the recent end; reinsertion keeps its original price. New insertions evict the oldest entry when full. Every LruCache command constructs a fresh empty cache with the new capacity, so resets discard all earlier keys and recency. A nonpositive capacity stores no entries. The command tester checks every lookup and erase result and rejects unknown operations.
timeComplexity: O(1) expected amortized time for lookup, insertion and erasure. Resetting drops the prior dictionary, taking O(q) time to release q live entries; over a sequence this cleanup is charged to their earlier insertions.
spaceComplexity: O(c + 1) live-entry storage for positive capacity c, with O(1) storage at nonpositive capacity. OrderedDict allocation can retain space proportional to the peak occupancy since the latest reset; a reset replaces that storage entirely.
